title: Deborah and Barak at the Kishon

named.name: Hazor
named.label: right
named.note: Jabin "king of Canaan" reigned in Hazor (4:2), the greatest city of Canaan, burned by Joshua (Joshua 11:10–13) and evidently rebuilt as a power again. The excavations show a great fire at the end of the Late Bronze Age; how the layers fit Joshua and Judges is debated.

named.name: Harosheth-hagoyim
named.label: left
named.site: unknown; perhaps in the Kishon gorge below Carmel
named.note: "Harosheth of the nations," Sisera's home and base. His 900 iron chariots came from here to the Kishon, and Barak pursued them back to it (4:2, 13, 16). Some read the name as "the forested land of the nations," a region rather than a town.

named.name: Palm of Deborah
named.label: right
named.site: between Ramah and Bethel, hill country of Ephraim
named.note: Deborah judged Israel under her palm tree between Ramah and Bethel (4:4–5). From here she summoned Barak, more than 100 km to the north, and went with him to Kedesh (4:6–9).

named.name: Kedesh
named.label: right
named.site: Khirbet Qedish, above the Sea of Galilee
named.note: Barak's home, "Kedesh in Naphtali" (4:6), where he called out Zebulun and Naphtali (4:10). This Kedesh, near Tabor and the tent of Heber, fits the story better than the great Kedesh in upper Galilee (Tel Kedesh).

named.name: Mount Tabor
named.label: above
named.note: The rounded mountain at the north-east corner of the Jezreel Valley. Barak gathered ten thousand men on it, safe from chariots, and charged down at Deborah's word: "Arise! For this is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hand" (4:14).

named.name: Kishon
named.label: below
named.site: Nahal Kishon, the stream of the Jezreel Valley
named.note: "The torrent Kishon swept them away" (5:21). The song tells of rain from heaven (5:4, 20): a cloudburst would turn the valley floor into deep mud, where chariots were useless.

named.name: Megiddo
named.label: left
named.note: "The kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo" (5:19): the battle was fought in the valley below these two cities.

named.name: Taanach
named.label: right
named.note: Eight km south-east of Megiddo, also on the edge of the valley (5:19).

named.name: Zaanannim
named.label: right
named.note: Heber the Kenite had separated from the other Kenites and pitched his tent "by the great tree of Zaanannim, near Kedesh" (4:11). Sisera fled here on foot, and Jael killed him with a tent peg (4:17–21).

moves.text: Barak calls up Zebulun and Naphtali at Kedesh and goes up to Mount Tabor with ten thousand men; Deborah goes with him
Sisera brings his 900 iron chariots from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Kishon
Barak charges down from Tabor; the LORD routs Sisera and his chariots
Barak pursues the chariots to Harosheth-hagoyim; not a man is left
Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael, near Kedesh

symbols.key: "The kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo… the torrent Kishon swept them away"
Jael kills Sisera in her tent

p: Sisera's strength was his nine hundred iron-fitted chariots (4:3), which ruled the flat Jezreel Valley. Barak waited on Mount Tabor, where chariots could not reach him. Deborah's song tells what turned the battle: "the clouds poured down water… the stars fought from the heavens… the torrent Kishon swept them away" (5:4, 20–21). In the mud of the valley floor the chariots became a trap.

The song names the tribes that came, Ephraim, Benjamin, Machir (Manasseh), Zebulun, Issachar and Naphtali, and those that stayed home: Reuben "among the sheepfolds," Gilead beyond the Jordan, Dan by the ships and Asher by the coast (5:14–18). Meroz is cursed "for they did not come to help the LORD" (5:23). The victory is the LORD's, and the honour goes to a woman, as Deborah said: Jael, "most blessed of women in tents" (4:9; 5:24).
